glossary.Bronchial dilation: Widening of the bronchi (the airways) beyond normal size.
glossary.Bronchi: The main airways branching from the trachea into each lung.
glossary.Mucus clearance: Removal of mucus from the airways by cilia and coughing.
glossary.Pneumonia: Infection of the lung tissue causing inflammation of the air sacs.
glossary.TB: Tuberculosis: infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis, often damaging the lungs.
glossary.Immunodeficiency: A weakened immune system, inherited or acquired, raising infection risk.
glossary.Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis: An allergic reaction in the airways to the fungus Aspergillus, usually in asthma or CF.
glossary.Rheumatoid arthritis: Autoimmune disease causing inflammation of the joints and sometimes the lungs.
glossary.Productive cough: A cough that brings up sputum.
glossary.Sputum: Mucus coughed up from the lower airways.
glossary.Inspiratory crackles: Crackling sounds heard on breathing in, from airways opening or secretions.
glossary.Wheeze: Whistling sound from air moving through narrowed airways.
glossary.Spirometry: A breathing test measuring how much and how fast air can be blown out.
glossary.FEV1: Forced expiratory volume in 1 second: air blown out in the first second.
glossary.FVC: Forced vital capacity: total air blown out after a full breath in.
glossary.Exocrine: Glands releasing secretions into ducts, such as pancreatic digestive enzymes.
glossary.Endocrine: Glands releasing hormones into the blood, such as pancreatic insulin.
glossary.Pancreatic dysfunction: The pancreas failing to make enough enzymes or insulin.
glossary.Sputum culture: Growing organisms from sputum in the lab to identify them and their antibiotic sensitivities.
glossary.Chest physiotherapy: Breathing and positioning techniques to help clear sputum from the lungs.
glossary.Inspiratory muscle training: Exercises against resistance to strengthen the breathing-in muscles.
glossary.Adjunct: An extra treatment added to the main one.
glossary.IV antibiotics: Antibiotics given directly into a vein.
glossary.Corticosteroids: Anti-inflammatory steroid drugs such as prednisolone.
glossary.Prophylactic: Given to prevent a problem rather than treat it.
glossary.Bronchodilators: Inhaled drugs that relax airway muscle to widen the airways.
glossary.Vaccination: Giving a vaccine to prevent infections such as flu and pneumococcus.
glossary.Massive haemoptysis: Coughing up a large, life-threatening amount of blood.
glossary.Lobectomy: Surgery to remove one lobe of a lung.
glossary.Colonisation: Organisms living in a site long-term, without necessarily causing acute infection.
glossary.Chloride channel: A membrane protein that lets chloride ions move across cells; draws water into mucus.
glossary.Cartilage: Firm connective tissue that supports the walls of the larger airways.
glossary.Inflammation: The body's response to injury or infection: swelling, immune cells and chemical signals.
